tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תְּפִלָּה לְיוֹם הַזִּכָּרוֹן וְיוֹם הָעַצְמָאוּת
A Prayer for Yom haZikaron and Yom ha-Atsma'ut 5785, by Rabbi Tzachi Lehman (Tzohar 2025)

tei:div.tei:head: A Prayer for Yom haZikaron and Yom ha-Atsma'ut 5785, by Rabbi Tzachi Lehman (Tzohar 2025)

tei:lg.tei:l: Our father in Heaven,
the Rock of Israel and our Redeemer.
We come before you
with tear-filled eyes
and a broken heart,
Yet believing in goodness
and in search of comfort.
The world’s evil forces have attacked us.
They have murdered and taken captive
men, women and children,
And wholly disgraced the image of God.
And in contrast to their destruction and thirst for evil...
Civilians and soldiers alike gave their lives.
With bravery, heroism and ultimate dedication
They went out to war.
And upheld the honor of the land and people of Israel.
Our hearts are awash in both pain and pride:
Pain for the horrific plagues we have endured.
Yet pride for the tremendous heroism we have witnessed.
And with a broken heart; a heart that still believes in goodness
We extend our hands towards You.
That You should fill us and the entire world
With comfort and hope.
With life and with peace.
Return all of our hostages
Heal all the wounded
Strengthen the unity among us.
And open our eyes
to the immense good which surrounds us.
Give us the strength
to overcome the pain and loss,
to assist all those in need
and to continue to build and heal
our beloved nation
And may we fullfill that which is written:
“Arise, shine, for your light has come,
and the glory of Hashem has risen upon you.” (Isaiah 60:1).
And we say Amen.
